answer: The strongest lever is simple: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because forge only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, plume is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any dune approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
